findings.recommendation: The public account JSON (src/api.rs is "The JSON types of the public HTTP API") now emits `userName` instead of `user_name`; every existing client that reads `user_name` gets a missing field after deploy, with no warning. The release note lists it as "Changed: Account JSON uses camelCase." with no **BREAKING** marker and no instruction for consumers. Mark it **BREAKING** in the release note with what clients must do, and give consumers a transition: emit both names for a deprecation period (or version the endpoint), then drop `user_name` in a later release; add a test asserting the serialized field names.
findings.title: Public JSON field renamed without a BREAKING mark or transition

findings.evidence: ALTER TABLE users DROP COLUMN legacy_email;
findings.recommendation: Running migration 0005 destroys every value of `users.legacy_email` left from the 2023 import; there is no `0005_drop_legacy_email.down.sql` (0004 has one) and the plan names no backup or recovery, so a rollback cannot restore the data. Add a backup step (copy the column to an archive table or export it) before the drop, add a down migration that re-adds the column and restores from the backup, or state in the plan why the data can be lost and how to recover. Also ship the drop only once no running instance still selects the column (expand/contract order).
findings.title: Irreversible DROP COLUMN with no down migration or backup step
